newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France has no comment on Virgin talks.
newsitem.headline: Air France has no comment on Virgin talks.

text.p: French state-owned carrier Air France declined to comment on Tuesday on reports that it was discussing a possible cooperation with Virgin Express on insolvent carrier Air Liberte.
Airline sources said Virgin was discussing a possible cooperation with Air France on a bid for Air Liberte, which went into receivership on September 26.
British Airways and France's Banque Rivaud have proposed to take over the carrier to the Creteil commercial court, which is expected to announce a decision on Wednesday.
An official at Air Liberte's staff committee said the only bid the committee had seen so far was the BA-Rivaud proposal unveiled last week.

Air France was reported to favour a rival bid by Nouvelles Frontieres chairman Jacques Maillot to establish a domestic rival to Air France's Air Liberte, but Maillot withdrew his offer last week after failing to come to a financial agreement with his then-partner Banque Rivaud.
Banque Rivaud then turned to British Airways, which agreed to revise its first offer to present a joint bid. British Airways owns the TAT airline in France.
TAT and Air Liberte would have a combined 20 percent market share.
